messages:
carla: quick heads-up — saw a 2.8x perf regression on Mistral-7B in the nightly run after the kernel-selector tweak. looks like FA/SDPA kernels aren’t being chosen when head_dim=80 so we fall back to matmul+masked-softmax. profiler attached.
ben: ugh. is the selector matching on head_dim % 16? iirc we added a stricter check last week.
dan: can you paste the profiler flame/profile snippet? also which commit?
carla: commit 9f3b2a1, selector change to prefer Triton batch-optimized kernels. profiler top stacks:
```
89.7%  slow_masked_softmax
  - aten::bmm (fallback path)
  - aten::softmax (masked)
8.5%  load_kv + copy_to_host
1.8%  dispatch_selector
```
eva: head_dim 80 is not a multiple of 16, right? FlashAttention expects head_dim % 8 == 0 (and often benefits from %16). if our selector requires %16 it will skip.
carla: head_dim=80 -> %16==0? actually 80%16==0 so it should match. hmm. the model's kv_dim per head seems 80, but effective kernel expects padded stride multiple of 128 because of vectorized loads on Ampere. selector is checking for align_bytes >= 128. wrong assumption.
ben: ah the alignment gate. that explains 2.8x. on Ampere we can often run with head_dim 80 using SDPA if we allow unaligned loads but with slower throughput; our conservative gate forced full fallback.
dan: is the masking bug we saw on Qwen related? last month we had masked softmax incorrectly applying causal mask when seq_len % 32 != 0. could be similar.
eva: i ran a quick local repro with mixtral-8x and toggled the gate:
```yaml
runtime.kernel_selector:
  prefer_flash: true
  require_align_bytes: 128 # current
  allow_unaligned: false # toggle to test
```
when allow_unaligned=true, FlashAttention path picks up and we get 1.05x vs baseline 1.0x; when false we fall back and see 2.7-3x slowdown.
carla: logs show fallback reason: "kernel_incompatible: mask_stride_mismatch" from selector. not a direct bug in FA but the runtime incorrectly marks mask_stride mismatch for head_dim 80 due to our pad-to-block heuristic.
ben: proposals: 1) relax align_bytes gate for Ampere/Trident architectures and add microbenchmark to ensure no silent correctness regressions; 2) add a tiny padding pass that pads kv cache widths to next vector multiple at runtime (cheap mem overhead) for models with nonstandard heads; 3) reintroduce a masking unit test that exercises odd seq_len/head_dim combos.
eva: +1 for padding pass. easy to implement: when head_dim % 16 != 0, allocate padded KV buffers (pad to next 16) and adjust stride. cheap and keeps FA path. we already do something similar for qkv packing in the onnx loader.
dan: padding pass will increase memory per request — need to add a warning to the telemetry and a config knob to disable per-model. also add batching heuristic: if batch*N_seq*pad_bytes grows past threshold, fall back to streaming or lower batching.
carla: agreed. immediate mitigation: flip selector to prefer_fallback=false for nightly to avoid regressions in customer runs. longer term: implement runtime pad + mask fix + unit tests.
infra-bot: deploy status: rolling kernel-selector revert to canary on cluster "staging" (deploy id d-2025-11-30-7).
eva: i'll prototype padding pass tonight and add unit tests for seq_len % 32 != 0 and head_dim in {64,80,96,128}. will also add a perf microbenchmark that runs matrix for head_dim in 1..256 to plot crossover.
ben: add an e2e replay test that uses a real Mistral mix of seq lengths from our production trace. ensure we capture KV cache cold starts + long streams.
carla: thanks. action items: @eva prototype pad+tests, @ben add replay suite, @dan add telemetry knob and rollout safety flag, i'll open PR to revert selector in canary. we'll sync tomorrow 10am. :thumbsup:
